title: WHO RESCUES WHOM
subtitle: 6 authorities turned exporter during Winter Storm Uri, February 2021, 5 turned importer

chart.x_label: Balancing authorities that flipped, and the event's grid; Winter Storm Uri, February 2021
chart.y_left_label: net exports, MWh a day (below zero: net imports)

callouts.label: ERCOT net flow, MWh a day

why: Of the 71 balancing authorities with flows on both the window and its baseline, 6 flipped from net importing to net exporting during Winter Storm Uri, February 2021 and 5 the other way; 58 kept their sign and 2 moved under 1,000 MWh a day both ways. ERCOT itself went from 512 MWh a day on the baseline to -9,652 in the window (a net importer during the event; positive is net export). The largest new exporter was PacifiCorp East: -357 MWh a day on the baseline, 11,611 in the window. The largest new importer was SPP: 6,239 on the baseline, -43,416 in the window. The biggest swing of all was PJM's, 175,325 MWh a day. A flip says who sent power the other way when it was scarce; it does not say why, and a tie-line's limit, a neighbour's own emergency or a scheduled outage can each move a sign.
footnote: Data: eia930_daily_interchange, EIA-930's daily interchange by pair of balancing authorities (EIA's Eastern-time days; a positive value is power from the row's authority to its neighbour), 16,474 rows read; EIA's region rows (CAL, CAR, CENT, FLA, MIDA, MIDW, NE, NW, NY, SE, SW, TEN, TEX, US48) left out. A pair's flow on a day is the mean of its two sides' reports where both are held (8,604 pair-days, 7,870 with both sides, 1,459 of those with the sides more than a tenth apart); an authority's day is the sum over its pairs (exports minus imports). Window: 2021-02-07 to 2021-02-24 (18 days), from event_window_daily's header (docs/methods/events.md). Baseline: the same calendar days 364 and 728 days earlier, 36 days, averaged where held. Flip: the sign of the baseline mean against the sign of the window mean; an authority under 1,000 MWh a day on both is 'small'. Every authority with days on both sides is a row; the chart shows the flipped ones and the event's grid, largest swing first, at most 14.
source_line: Source: EIA-930 (Hourly Electric Grid Monitor), daily interchange; ERW tables eia930_daily_interchange, event_window_daily.
